subject: Tranche-swap hedge for dedicated onramp — OEM queue contingency
body:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ops@cloudwave.com, sales@oemsystems.com, nina@nimbus.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Tranche-swap hedge for dedicated onramp — OEM queue contingency

Team / partners,

Quick summary: Nimbus (DEAL-9341) wants a 3-phase Dedicated onramp starting Feb 2027. OEM is signaling a 20–28 week lead time for full-slab shipments; CloudWave can provide short-term burst capacity but at premium pricing. To avoid missing the customer SLA, I'm proposing a tranche-swap hedge: OEM commits to staggered partial shipments (40% / 30% / 30%) with escrowed slot priority and a cloud backfill commitment for the first 8 weeks.

Attached: OEM_quote_v2.pdf, capacity_tranche_matrix.xlsx

Asks:
- OEM (sales): confirm whether you can commit to tranche deliveries and provide firm milestones for each tranche (dates + partial-acceptance criteria).
- CloudWave: confirm burst pricing and the minimum booking window for 8-week coverage; can you guarantee region us-west availability?
- Internal (Karthik/Ben/Laura): review the attached matrix and flag any operational risk (networking, staging, licensing) we should put in contract.

If OEM can commit to tranche shipments we can:
- Put a DocuSign amendment for tranche acceptance and escrowed lead-time credits.
- Use CloudWave as a documented fallback so Sales can offer the Feb SLA without overcommitting HW.

Thanks — aiming to lock principles by EOD Monday so Legal can draft amendment.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OEM_quote_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]
[Attachment: capacity_tranche_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)]

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ops@cloudwave.com, sales@oemsystems.com, nina@nimbus.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tranche-swap hedge for dedicated onramp — OEM queue contingency

Mina — thanks for the clear ask. A few operational notes from infra/serving perspective:

1) Tranche acceptance criteria: we should define KV-cache warmup windows (48–72h), a reduced-traffic smoke window per tranche, and an ingress capacity gating rule so we don't cut over full production until last tranche is validated.
2) Staging pools: partial shipments will need a temporary routing policy so new hardware is prefixed into a staging pool (dedicated:sprint-1) before joining the customer's pinned pool.
3) Licensing/software: OEM firmware parity matters for cluster-level quant optimizations. If firmware versions differ between tranches we may need to pin a compatible software image and delay certain optimizations.

I've annotated the capacity_tranche_matrix.xlsx with comments — high risk items in red.

Karthik
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference

From: Alejandro Ruiz <sales@oemsystems.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ops@cloudwave.com, nina@nimbus.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 08:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Tranche-swap hedge for dedicated onramp — OEM queue contingency

Mina and team,

Appreciate the proposal. We can support a tranche-based delivery for Nimbus provided we get an early slot deposit and a clear acceptance schedule. Proposed cadence:
- Tranche A (40%): target ship week starting 2027-02-07 — partial-acceptance (hardware + basic firmware)
- Tranche B (30%): target ship week starting 2027-03-14 — staging validation complete
- Tranche C (30%): target ship week starting 2027-04-25 — final parity and QA

We will include escrowed slot priority in the amended PO and can provide serial-level shipment manifests one week before each tranche ships. We need clarity on the cloud backfill window (weeks covered) and whether Redwood will accept split acceptance (partial invoice on tranche A).

Attached: OEM_quote_v2.pdf (updated margin notes)

Regards,
Alejandro Ruiz
OEM Systems — Strategic Accounts
[Attachment: OEM_quote_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ops@cloudwave.com, sales@oemsystems.com, nina@nimbus.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tranche-swap hedge for dedicated onramp — OEM queue contingency

Quick commercial thoughts:
- If we accept partial invoicing per tranche we should build in a clawback credit if the final tranche slips >4 weeks.
- CloudWave pricing for an 8-week burst (us-west) will be acceptable if their effective per-token cost delta is <1.8x our committed rate; otherwise we need a negotiated customer credit in the SOW.
- Laura, can you confirm whether Finance is comfortable with slot deposit terms vs. our cashflow for DEC/JAQ?

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tranche-swap hedge for dedicated onramp — OEM queue contingency

Thanks all for the quick turn. Summary & next steps: 

1) OEM (Alejandro) — confirmed tranche schedule. Please send the updated PO with the escrow clause and partial manifest cadence by COB Wed (2026-11-17).
2) CloudWave — please provide a binding 8-week short-term pricing sheet for us-west by Tue EOD (2026-11-17) so Sales can finalize offer language.
3) Karthik — we'll use your gating checklist (KV warmup + staging pool policy). Please attach the annotated matrix into the HubSpot deal (link above) so Legal/CS can reference it in the amendment.
4) Ben/Laura/Finance — Ben's clawback proposal looks right; Laura, confirm deposit tolerance.

If we can get those three items by 11/17 we can sign a DocuSign amendment and publish a canary rollout plan for Feb.

— Mina
Head of Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference
